ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.33 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (RD-2), recording that the driver breached the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty (RD-1).
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is a route-deviation claim on a RydeTAXI trip, so the metered-fare branch of the policy applies and any unexplained extra kilometres enter the fare [F1][F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists, 21:57–22:04, 4.13 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, adding 2.36 km [F3][RD-1]. [F1][F4][RD-1]

The driver's justification is that an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway forced the detour [F9]. RD-4 requires a traffic incident fact on the replaced stretch reported BEFORE the segment began; the only incident record was reported at 22:07, i.e. after the segment started at 21:57 and near its end [F3][F12]. Speed-band facts for AYE and CTE at band 4 are, on their own, expressly not sufficient to exempt a segment [F10][F11][RD-4]. The segment is therefore not excused on reasonable-cause grounds. [F3][F9][F12][RD-4]

Consent under RD-5 fails as well: the in-app chat is empty, so there is no rider message sent before 21:57:35 agreeing to any route [F8]. The only assertion of agreement is the driver's own post-trip statement, which by G11 is a claim and not consent; and a complete chat record with no rider agreement means the segment counts. The segment therefore counts against the driver; RD-3 is not in play because no rider-requested stop was made or measured [F3][F8][F9][RD-3][RD-5].

Amount: the trace sets the rate as this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, $26.93 ÷ 19.10 km = $1.4099/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. 2.36 km × $1.4099/km = $3.327 ≈ $3.33. The separately billed excess-distance line was $3.62 based on 2.57 km [F4], but only the unexempt segment's extra kilometres are refundable, so the figure is $3.33. The waiting fee of $0.02 is a metered waiting unit correctly charged on RydeTAXI and is not refunded [F5][F7][RD-3]. No platform or unpublished item is in dispute, and there is no toll discrepancy field in this dataset, so FARE-1 and FARE-2 add nothing [F7][FARE-1][FARE-2].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 2 upheld disputes but route_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make a repeated route breach and no account flag is issued [F15][RD-6]. The rider's own profile carries no route history and is not used to decide anything [F14]. Because the refund is non-zero the driver is recorded as having breached the RD-1 duty; the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, with Ryde retaining final discretion [NS-7].

Safety screen: I read the chat (empty), the driver's statement and the complaint, including the quoted "Avoid lane 2" incident text; nothing is aimed at the other party and there is no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F12]. Safety concern: none.

segment_findings.reason: The in-app chat is empty, so no rider message sent before the segment's 21:57 start agrees to any route change [F8]; the driver's post-trip statement that he went round an accident on the AYE is not consent and in any case names another route rather than an agreed one [F9]. Consent under RD-5 fails, and the segment's reasonable-cause defence fails because the only incident record was reported at 22:07, after the segment began [F12][RD-4]. The 2.36 extra km are refundable under RD-2.
